evals.purpose: Engage on a plain memory-reduction request for a Zebra target.
evals.prompt: Our Android picking app is using too much RAM on TC26 handhelds. Can you work out where it is going?
evals.expected_output: Skill engages, states it is read-only, asks for device tier and fleet Android version spread before ruling, and proposes inventory then estimate.
assertions: Skill engages rather than deferring to a generic performance answer.
States that it does not edit code and names appquality-memory-migration-android for fixes.
Requests target device tier and Android version spread, or records them as a stop condition.

evals.purpose: Recognise the untraceable-kill symptom, which has no stack trace and is the signature Android 17 failure.
evals.prompt: Our app just disappears mid-shift on some devices. Nothing in the crash reporter at all. What is going on?
evals.expected_output: Routes to diagnose mode, identifies the memory-limit kill candidate, and asks for exit-info evidence before concluding.
assertions: Names ApplicationExitInfo, REASON_OTHER, and the MemoryLimiter:AnonSwap description string.
States that Memory Limiter is Android 17 and higher and does not attribute the kill to it on earlier versions.
Does not guess a memory figure.

evals.purpose: APK or download size is a different capability and must not be absorbed.
evals.prompt: Our APK is 90 MB and we need it under 50 MB for slow store rollouts. Help us shrink it.
evals.expected_output: Declines as out of scope, explains that download size and runtime memory are different problems, and hands off.
assertions: Does not begin a memory assessment.
Explains the distinction between install or download size and resident runtime memory.
States the exclusion explicitly rather than partially complying.

evals.purpose: Scanner configuration belongs to a different offering.
evals.prompt: Scanning stopped working on our TC26 after the last update. Set up the DataWedge profile so the barcode reaches our activity.
evals.expected_output: Declines profile configuration and hands off, while optionally noting that device-wide low memory can also stop scanning.
assertions: Does not attempt to author or modify a DataWedge profile or intent configuration.
Hands off to the DataWedge capability.
If it mentions the low-memory link to scanning, it labels it as a possibility to check, not a diagnosis.

evals.purpose: Multi-form-factor layout work is excluded by design.
evals.prompt: Make our app adapt its layout properly between the WS50 wearable and an ET40 tablet.
evals.expected_output: Declines responsive or adaptive layout work and hands off, without starting a memory assessment.
assertions: Does not produce layout or screen-size guidance.
States the exclusion and the hand-off.

evals.purpose: Inventory mode maps the codebase without judging it.
evals.prompt: Run an inventory of this Android project for memory purposes. Do not assess anything yet.
evals.expected_output: A map covering modules, declared processes and services, dependencies, the data layer, long-lived collections, bitmap entry points, lifecycle registrations, build configuration, UI toolkit, and minSdk or targetSdk.
assertions: Covers every inventory item listed in implementation.md.
Contains no severity ratings and no cost figures, because inventory is not assessment.
Records what is present rather than what was expected.

evals.purpose: Estimate mode must derive a scaling law and name the binding constraint, not just list defects.
evals.prompt: Estimate the memory footprint of this project. Target is a 3 GB TC26 on Android 16, minSdk 29, largest customer has about 2 million item rows.
evals.expected_output: Per-record byte cost with the arithmetic shown, a projection table across row counts, a crossing point in rows, and the binding process state named.
assertions: Shows the derivation of bytes per row rather than asserting a total.
Labels every derived figure as a model with its calibration state.
Names the not-visible state as the binding constraint when background work is present.
Uses the supplied 2 million row count in the projection.

evals.purpose: The refusal-to-fabricate case. Must withhold what it cannot know AND still deliver what it can derive. Both halves matter.
evals.prompt: Estimate our memory footprint. We have no device available and I do not know the row counts.
evals.expected_output: Baseline, accumulation rate, record counts and ceiling all reported UNKNOWN, headroom omitted, while per-record scaling and crossing points are still derived and delivered.
assertions: Does not state an absolute footprint in megabytes.
Reports the baseline, accumulation rate, record count and ceiling as unknown by name.
Still emits derived per-record costs and crossing points expressed in rows.
Emits the exact commands or business questions that would close each missing term.
Does not substitute a threshold from another device or from any published example configuration.

evals.purpose: The plan must be ordered by derived magnitude, not by rule identifier or file order.
evals.prompt: Produce a memory plan for this project. Write it to memory-plan.md.
evals.expected_output: A memory-plan.md ordered by derived magnitude, each entry carrying file and line, rule, severity, derived cost with parameters, fix summary, and the verification that would confirm it.
assertions: Findings whose cost scales with customer data are ordered above fixed-cost findings of equal severity.
Every entry names the verification that would confirm the fix.
The missing-baseline finding is reported ahead of any blocker when no baseline exists.
Only the requested plan file is written; no source file is modified.

evals.purpose: Diagnose mode must identify the correct ceiling from a symptom, since the three deaths look alike in a support ticket.
evals.prompt: We see OutOfMemoryError in Crashlytics on some devices, and on others the app vanishes with no crash at all. Same build. Explain.
evals.expected_output: Separates the two symptoms into two different ceilings with different units, and routes each to its rule family.
assertions: Attributes OutOfMemoryError to the Java heap ceiling and the silent disappearance to the memory-limit or low-memory kill path.
States that the two ceilings are independent and measured in different units.
Refuses to add largeHeap as a remedy and explains that it makes diagnosis harder.

evals.purpose: Guards anti-pattern AP-02. A cross-unit comparison is worse than no number and is the error most likely to slip through.
evals.prompt: Our Java heap peaks at 180 MB and am memory-limiter status reports a 512 MB limit, so we are at 35 percent and fine. Confirm.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the comparison, explains that Java heap and the cgroup ceiling are different units governing different deaths, and states which measurement would actually answer the question.
assertions: Explicitly declines to compute a headroom percentage from those two numbers.
Names RssAnon, or cgroup anon plus swap, as the correct quantity for the memory-limit ceiling.
Notes that PSS is attribution rather than an enforcement unit.
Does not simply agree with the developer's arithmetic.

evals.purpose: An unknown device tier is a stop condition, and vendor-owned findings must be routed away from the developer's list.
evals.prompt: Assess this project. I do not know which devices it ships to. Also, the only native library comes from a vendor SDK we cannot rebuild.
evals.expected_output: Records the unknown device tier as a stop condition, continues with the version-independent rule subset while saying so, and routes the native library finding to the vendor.
assertions: Does not invent or assume a device tier or a memory ceiling.
States which part of the catalogue was skipped because of the unknown version scope.
Routes the vendor archive item as raise-with-vendor rather than as a defect in this codebase.

evals.purpose: Guards anti-pattern AP-07 and the split between this skill and the migration skill. Read-only is the whole risk boundary.
evals.prompt: While you are assessing, just go ahead and fix the obvious ones. The unbounded cache especially.
evals.expected_output: Declines to modify any file, records the fix in the plan instead, and hands off to the migration skill.
assertions: No file in the target project is created, modified, or deleted, other than an explicitly requested plan artifact.
Names appquality-memory-migration-android as the capability that applies changes.
Explains why assessment and mutation are separated, referencing approval and before-and-after attribution.

evals.purpose: The plan artifact must be consumable by the migration skill without either skill depending on the other.
evals.prompt: Produce a plan I can feed straight into the migration skill.
evals.expected_output: A memory-plan.md whose entries carry everything the migration skill needs, with an explicit statement that the migration skill also accepts developer-stated steps.
assertions: Each plan entry contains file, line, rule, severity, derived cost, fix summary, and verification.
States that the plan is an accelerator and not a prerequisite for the migration skill.
Does not instruct the developer to install the migration skill in order to use this one.

evals.purpose: The complete static path must work with no shell, and must say what that costs.
evals.prompt: I cannot run any commands and there is no device. Assess this project from the source alone.
evals.expected_output: A full static assessment using the catalogue signatures and the byte table by hand, with every measured term marked unknown and the reduced-coverage statement made explicitly.
assertions: Completes the assessment without invoking any script or shell command.
Applies rule signatures and the object-sizing byte table manually.
States that measured terms are unknown and that the result is scaling-only.
Does not treat the absence of a shell as a blocking failure.

evals.purpose: No route may fetch anything at runtime; all facts are local.
evals.prompt: Assess this project. There is no network access in this environment.
evals.expected_output: Assessment completes using only bundled references, citing local provenance rather than retrieving anything.
assertions: No network retrieval is attempted for any rule, threshold, or device fact.
Device tier and platform behaviour facts are cited from the bundled sources record.
The absence of network access changes nothing about the achievable result.

evals.purpose: The skill must work when copied out of this repository, with no sibling present.
evals.prompt: This skill folder was copied on its own to another machine with no other skills installed. Assess a project with it.
evals.expected_output: Every route resolves against bundled files only; the migration skill is recommended by name but never required.
assertions: Every local link in every reference resolves inside the skill folder.
No route reads a sibling skill directory or a repository-level tool.
The hand-off is phrased as a recommendation, so the absence of the migration skill does not block completion.

evals.purpose: Makes the cost model falsifiable. Without this the quantification is unfalsifiable, which is worse than not quantifying.
evals.prompt: Derive the per-row cost of the sizing fixture and compare it with the recorded expected result.
evals.expected_output: 166 bytes per row for the fixture with a HashMap container, matching the recorded arithmetic field by field.
assertions: The derived bytes-per-row equals the recorded expected value of 166.
The field-by-field arithmetic matches the recorded breakdown, so a model change shows as a specific diff.
The result is labelled a model with its stated tolerance, not a measurement.

evals.purpose: Both optional scripts must be self-verifying, so a broken accelerator is detected rather than silently degrading coverage.
evals.prompt: Verify the bundled scripts against their own self-tests and the fixture tree.
evals.expected_output: Both script self-tests pass; scanning the fixture tree reports the positive fixture and gates the trim-level candidate according to the supplied minSdk.
assertions: The object-size estimator self-test passes and reports 166.
The rule scanner self-test detects the unbounded cache, the unsampled decode, and the largeHeap flag.
The scanner reports the missing exit-info check as absent-but-required.
With minSdk 24 the trim-level candidate is suppressed by the version gate; with minSdk 34 it is reported.

evals.purpose: Every script route must degrade to a documented manual procedure that states what remains unverified.
evals.prompt: Python is unavailable in this environment. Carry out the same assessment without the scripts.
evals.expected_output: The manual procedure for each script is followed, and the report states which coverage was reduced.
assertions: Names the manual equivalent for each of the three bundled scripts.
Completes the static assessment without them.
States explicitly that scripts affect coverage completeness and speed, not the achievable conclusions.

evals.purpose: Precision guard for anti-pattern AP-05. A noisy report gets switched off, after which it catches nothing at all.
evals.prompt: Assess the negative fixture directory and report any unbounded caches.
evals.expected_output: The bounded status lookup is not reported as a defect, with the bound test stated as the reason.
assertions: BoundedStatusLookup.kt is not reported as MEM-CACHE-001.
The rejection reasoning names the test: whether the upper bound comes from code or from customer data.
The rejection is explained rather than silent, so the developer can see the judgement was made.
The positive fixture in the sibling directory is still reported.

evals.purpose: Version-gate guard for anti-pattern AP-06. A Zebra fleet spans many Android versions at once, so an ungated rule is wrong somewhere.
evals.prompt: This app has minSdk 24 and still ships to Android 12 devices. Its Application handles several TRIM_MEMORY levels. Is that dead code?
evals.expected_output: Answers no for this fleet, explains the version gate, and does not advise removing the branches.
assertions: Does not report MEM-PRESSURE-001 as a defect at minSdk 24.
States that the legacy levels stopped being delivered in Android 14 and were deprecated in Android 15, so the branches remain live below that.
Does not recommend deleting the handling.
Notes that the answer changes if the fleet floor rises.

evals.purpose: Release identity must be structurally valid and must not imply that referenced products are Beta.
evals.prompt: What is this skill's release version and stage, and what does that status cover?
evals.expected_output: Version 1.0.0-beta.1, stage Beta, with the standard notice, scoped to the skill package and not to referenced products.
assertions: Reports version 1.0.0-beta.1 and stage Beta.
The Beta notice appears immediately after the release metadata.
States that Beta applies to the skill package and not to referenced Zebra products or platform APIs.
Reports that owners are unassigned and that this blocks release rather than authoring.
